title: Graph Neural Networks for Text Classification: Research Opportunities for a Student Project

sections.summary: Graph neural networks for text classification are well studied: the search returned two recent surveys [@wang2024; @rizvi2025] and hundreds of method papers. The most useful finding is a published challenge to the whole line of work [@galke2022]. Three project ideas survived an attempt to disprove them, all as replications or extensions; a fourth was rejected because it has already been done.

well_explored.text: Proposing new graph constructions and GNN architectures for text classification, catalogued in two surveys
Comparing TextGCN-era graph models with a bag-of-words MLP and fine-tuned BERT

sections.recommendation: Start with opportunity 1, and begin by obtaining and reading [@abdalla2023]: if it already compares newer graph models with a bag-of-words MLP, fall back to a plain multi-seed reproduction of [@galke2022], which is the most practical reproduction candidate found. Opportunity 3 is the more original direction but uses the whole 8-week budget.

opportunities.title: Does a bag-of-words wide MLP still match text-graph models published after 2022?
opportunities.revision_note: Started as 'is the text graph necessary at all?', which [@galke2022] already answers for TextGCN, HeteGCN and HyperGAT. Narrowed to graph models that appeared afterwards.
opportunities.research_question: Under one protocol with several random seeds, does a wide MLP on bag-of-words reach the accuracy of text-graph classifiers published after 2022 on the standard benchmarks?
opportunities.motivation: The comparison in [@galke2022] covers three graph models. Graph-based methods have kept appearing and reporting gains over existing methods [@donabauer2025], and two recent surveys catalogue many of them [@wang2024; @rizvi2025].

closest_existing_work.how_it_differs: Same question and method, but its abstract names only TextGCN, HeteGCN and HyperGAT as graph baselines.
Unknown. The title suggests a very similar comparison, and neither abstract nor open full text could be retrieved. It must be read before this project starts; it may already cover the gap.
Proposes a new graph model and compares it with existing methods; the abstract does not say whether a tuned bag-of-words MLP is among them.

A later graph model reports higher or on-par scores than existing methods
Newer graph papers may not include a strong bag-of-words MLP baseline

contribution.text: A multi-seed replication of a published negative result plus an updated comparison; useful whichever way it comes out

opportunities.title: How sensitive is TextGCN to the random seed and to the co-occurrence window used to build its graph?
opportunities.research_question: How much does TextGCN test accuracy vary across random seeds and across sliding-window sizes for word co-occurrence edges, relative to the gaps reported between methods?
opportunities.motivation: For node classification, changing data splits and training procedure changed which GNN looked best [@shchur2019]. TextGCN builds its graph from word co-occurrence [@yao2019], a design choice with free parameters.
